summary: The claim and proof are correct. The specialization of the accepted arithmetic fact preserves its support, coefficient, and original normalizer, and its hypotheses hold because Q >= 2ab implies Q >= max(a,b). The arithmetic bounds make every height in the required upper half occupied and justify the factor 1/6 in the comparison inequality. The geometric comparison law, both tilt cases, integer thresholds, block count, and blockwise estimates establish the stated e^{-13}/[216(m+1)] bound. The selected endpoints lie in the required range, and the final uniform-product domination uses the full original support and normalizer. Smallest admissible parameters, unit weights, equality at Q = 2ab, the tilt-case boundary, and arbitrarily large tilt cause no exception.
